units.teachingGoal: Preserve Ali's complete practical, information-judgment and participation reasons to care without beginning concept instruction.
questionsAnswered: Why is this book worth reading?

sections.title: Why AI Fundamentals matters to you
sections.teachingGoal: Preserve Ali's authored Introduction and reader relationship.
relationshipsAdded: Understanding supports better use, better judgment and informed participation.
questionsAnswered: Why should I understand AI without a technical background?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can name the reason that matters most to her.

units.teachingGoal: Build the principal AI families in the order their mechanisms and history make understandable, then show which relationships nest and which overlap.
questionsAnswered: What is AI?
How did rule-based AI lead to machine learning and today's systems?
How do the main current and proposed AI labels fit together?

sections.title: Start here: what is artificial intelligence?
sections.teachingGoal: Give a zero-prerequisite meaning for AI through an actual photo-search system.
relationshipsAdded: AI is the broad field, not one product or method.
questionsAnswered: What does AI mean in this book?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can identify the information, task and worked-out result in an ordinary AI interaction.

sections.title: First came AI built from human knowledge
sections.teachingGoal: Explain linked expert knowledge and rule-based reasoning while excluding trivial automation.
relationshipsAdded: Human experts supply the knowledge; the system reasons across linked rules in a bounded domain.
questionsAnswered: Why can an expert system count as AI?
Why is one automatic threshold not a useful AI example?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader distinguishes a linked expert system from a single business rule.

sections.title: Machine learning lets the computer find patterns in examples
sections.teachingGoal: Explain the change from supplied knowledge to learned patterns using an actual spam system.
relationshipsAdded: Machine learning is one major approach inside AI; not all AI is machine learning.
questionsAnswered: What changes when a system learns from examples?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader explains training as the study period and new-case use as the work period.

sections.title: Predictive AI uses patterns to estimate a new case
sections.teachingGoal: Connect classification, numerical prediction, ranking and recommendation through actual deployed-system patterns.
relationshipsAdded: Predictive systems estimate something about a new case; several linked estimates may support one visible recommendation.
questionsAnswered: What does predictive AI produce?
Why is a recommendation not certainty?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader traces an actual streaming recommendation through estimate, rank and recommend.

sections.title: Deep learning made much more complicated patterns possible
sections.teachingGoal: Explain neural networks and true AI-machine-learning-deep-learning nesting without brain mysticism.
relationshipsAdded: Deep learning is a type of machine learning, which is an approach inside AI.
questionsAnswered: How is deep learning related to machine learning?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can draw the three true nested families.

sections.title: Generative AI creates new content
sections.teachingGoal: Explain the new-content job and separate visible generation from internal next-piece prediction.
relationshipsAdded: Generative AI commonly uses deep learning; internal prediction supports a distinct visible generation job.
questionsAnswered: What makes an output generative?
Why can a generative model also make predictions internally?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader distinguishes estimating an existing email's category from producing a new email.

sections.title: Multimodal, agentic and embodied systems add new capabilities
sections.teachingGoal: Teach information-form, repeated-action and physical-world properties in separate consecutive explanations.
relationshipsAdded: The three labels describe different properties and may overlap generative or predictive work.
questionsAnswered: What does multimodal add?
What makes a complete system agentic?
What makes AI embodied?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can apply each label to an actual product without turning them into intelligence levels.

sections.title: Specialised, general-purpose, AGI and ASI describe breadth claims
sections.teachingGoal: Move from current bounded and broad-use systems to disputed and hypothetical categories with full names before acronyms.
relationshipsAdded: General-purpose current systems are not thereby AGI; AGI is disputed and ASI is hypothetical.
questionsAnswered: What would AGI require beyond broad current usefulness?
What does ASI propose?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader explains AGI and ASI without treating either as a current product or inevitable next step.

sections.title: Put the labels together and check the story
sections.teachingGoal: Separate true nesting from overlapping system properties and test transfer on a new consequential case.
relationshipsAdded: AI contains machine learning contains deep learning; other labels answer different questions and can overlap.
questionsAnswered: Can I reconstruct, explain and use the relationships on an unfamiliar product?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader completes Recognise, Explain, Draw and Use tasks with reasoned answers.
